So I added a team game where everybody gets a role: one holds the map, one reads clues, one runs. Nobody can hide in a corner. I'm glad I checked it in my head first. Ramya.

passage: Party notes, Friday evening. Tonight Trisha sat with her eyes closed and walked me through her party in her head. 'Four o'clock, everyone comes. Four-fifteen, musical chairs. Five, cake. Six, home.' Then she stopped. 'But Bidisha doesn't talk to anyone. In musical chairs she'll just stand at the side.' She thought for a while and added a team game: building the tallest tower from newspaper, with a job for everyone: a roller, a taper, a holder, a builder. 'Bidisha can be the holder. Nobody has to talk much.' I didn't suggest a thing. I've bought extra newspaper and tape.

What was Trisha feeling when she stopped at Bidisha?

qa.q: How might Bidisha experience the newspaper tower game?
qa.a: As the holder, Bidisha gets a clear job without having to talk much, so Bidisha may feel included and comfortable.

passage:
Wednesday night
Party on Saturday! Tonight I lay in bed and played it like a film in my head. Guests arrive at 4. Balloons. Then a relay race in the courtyard. Then cake, then pass the parcel, then home at 6:30. It looked perfect... until I pictured my cousin Jyoti. She's so shy she hid behind Masi all through my last party. In a relay she'd just stand there. So I added one game: a team puppet show, with jobs: one to hold the curtain, one to move the puppets, one to do the sounds, one to clap the signals. Jyoti can do the sounds from behind the curtain. Nobody has to look at her. Masi always says, 'Vasudha, look after Jyoti.' I think she'll like this.

qa.q: What job did Vasudha plan for Jyoti?
qa.a: Doing the sounds from behind the curtain.

qa.q: Why did Vasudha add the puppet show?
qa.a: She felt concerned that shy Jyoti would just stand there in a relay, and hoped Jyoti would enjoy a role behind the curtain.

qa.q: What might Vasudha also plan for when Jyoti first arrives?
qa.a: Meeting Jyoti at the gate and giving her a small task at once; walking through the party in her head is what showed this gap.

qa.q: How might Jyoti feel at the party with this plan?
qa.a: Jyoti can join in without being looked at, so she may feel safer and more included than at the last party.
